diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: At least 10 protest gatherings were held today, Monday, 25 Aban, in the cities of Kermanshah, Sanandaj, Isfahan, Bijar, Tehran, Hamedan, Ilam, and Borujerd. Retired telecommunications workers demanded the implementation of regulation 89/24 and salary adjustments. Additionally, water drainage workers in Bandar Mahshahr and national housing applicants in Nishapur protested job uncertainty and delays in unit delivery.

The death toll from the overturning of the bus carrying employees of the Dehloran gas refinery has reached 13 with the death of another injured person. In a separate incident, three workers at a factory on the Shiraz to Jahrom route suffered gas poisoning and were transferred to the hospital.

The New York Times reported that US and Israeli airstrikes on the Islamic Republic's missile facilities raised the possibility of a connection between Iran's extensive dam and water transfer projects and the country's military needs. Seven experts told the newspaper that underground military facilities near dams could provide stable access to water and electricity for missile bases. The newspaper emphasized that due to the secrecy of Iran's missile program, this potential connection has not yet been proven.

Mahsa Nouri, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, went on a hunger strike on Monday, 25 Aban, protesting the lack of attention to her demands, including the denial of parole and refusal to grant her leave. This news was reported to Harana by a source close to her family.

The website DownDetector has recorded over 3,300 disruption reports related to Chase Bank and about 800 reports related to Bank of America and Wells Fargo. Chase Bank has confirmed issues with its online banking services and stated it is working to resolve the disruption. The fintech company Plaid announced that its connections with Chase are disrupted, affecting communication channels and API requests, and the issue is still under investigation.

In continued security pressures on Baháʼís, intelligence agents searched the homes of five Baháʼí families in Semnan and arrested three people. Also, a Baháʼí citizen in Qaemshahr was sentenced to three years in prison and eight years of deprivation of social rights, and the two-year prison sentence of another Baháʼí citizen in Tehran was confirmed. It was reported that agents arrested Khanjani after beating him and confiscated the family's phones and laptops.

The United States Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt is present in the area under its command as part of a planned mission. According to CENTCOM, the aircraft carrier passed through the Indian Ocean on Sunday, November 15.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, announced that the Strait of Hormuz will not return to its pre-war status and will remain closed until the United States accepts the conditions of the Islamic Republic. He said if the United States does not accept the Islamic Republic's conditions, the strait will remain closed, and the presence of foreign forces in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman is a threat to regional security that must end. He also added that any renewed military action against the Islamic Republic will be met with a stronger response.

Varash Nowshahr defeated Palayesh Gaz Ilam 1-0 in the tenth week of the women's Premier League. With this win, Varash Nowshahr reached 9 points and moved up to sixth place in the standings. After the match, Varash Nowshahr players performed the Mazani dance.
Fardad Farahzad reported in Audio Version 24 that the largest U.S. military deployment in the Persian Gulf since the Iraq War has occurred.

The second branch of the Karaj Revolutionary Court sentenced Homayoun Shabankareh, a 22-year-old environmental activist, to death on charges of espionage. The judge issued the sentence based on confessions reportedly obtained under torture. Shabankareh was held in solitary confinement for over 130 days after being arrested by the IRGC intelligence.

Mansheh Amir, a Middle East expert, said severe disagreements between Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eizenkot have darkened the prospects of forming a national unity government in Israel. He added Netanyahu and his allies have raised issues of election fraud, Arab party participation, and the military threat of the Islamic Republic, but distrust between the two factions remains an obstacle to agreement. Amir also said Naftali Bennett may negotiate with Netanyahu and Eizenkot could form a coalition without Arab parties, and a new election is not unlikely.

Iranian media quoted Ali Pourmand, head of the medical committee of the Tehran Football Board, saying that holding any football training or matches in Tehran province on Tuesday, 26 Aban 1405 is prohibited. This comes after football training and matches were also canceled earlier this week in Tehran due to air pollution.

Behnam Taleblu said the Islamic Republic, after recent wars and a reduction in its nuclear capability, seeks to increase nuclear and missile threats against the international community. He added that Tehran is trying to extend the range of its missiles and expand its threats beyond the region. Taleblu considered the summit of the US, Russia, and China leaders related to the formation of a new global order and said Gulf countries seek security guarantees and economic reconstruction and do not fully trust the US strategy.

Morad Vaisi, senior analyst at Iran International, said the possible decision of Trump to attack the Islamic Republic depends on various factors, including the positions of advisors, Arab countries and Israel, the behavior of the Islamic Republic, the ability to maintain the US military posture in the region, the short time left until the new Congress starts, negotiations with China and Russia, and the consequences of retaliatory attacks by the Islamic Republic.

Morad Veysi, senior analyst at Iran International, said that the people of Iran are determined to overthrow the Islamic Republic regardless of Trump's decisions or political developments in Israel. He added that the people's expectation from the international community, especially the US and Israel, is to weaken the repression structure so they can achieve their goal with minimal cost and damage.

Donald Trump announced that he will discuss the Islamic Republic, the Ukraine war, and nuclear disarmament with the presidents of China and Russia. At the same time, JD Vance, the US Vice President, said the Trump administration will not allow the war with the Islamic Republic to become a long-term commitment for the United States.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported receiving a report of an incident 13 kilometers north of Khasab in Oman. According to the report, an oil tanker stopped working after an attack caused a fire in its engine room while passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

Peyman Hadadi, CEO of Persepolis, said that the advertisement for the sale of Amirhossein Mahmoudi in the newspaper was intended to show that there were interested parties and they did not intend to sell him. Hadadi added that any offer for Mahmoudi from Tuesday would be considered inducement, and this was a collective decision by the club's managers. He also said that Mahmoudi has two more seasons left on his contract with Persepolis, his contract is low, but they were seeking to increase it and have rewarded him for his national team call-up.

The Kuwaiti representative at the UN meeting on a Middle East free of weapons of mass destruction rejected the Islamic Republic's positions regarding attacks on US bases in the region and asked whether the residential neighborhoods and civilian facilities in Kuwait that were attacked are also US bases. He considered these positions an obvious attempt to shirk Tehran's responsibility for attacks against the sovereignty and territorial integrity of these countries.

A Turkish defense company has announced the development of a system that can disrupt the operation of dozens of drones simultaneously and within seconds. According to the company, the new system targets the electronic equipment of drones using powerful electromagnetic waves and is part of the "Steel Dome" project, a multi-layered air defense system of Turkey.

The Netherlands national team experienced its worst defeat since 1959 by losing 5-0 to Germany in the UEFA Nations League. This loss is one of the 10 heaviest defeats in Dutch history and the first time in nearly 70 years that the Netherlands lost by five goals or more. Previously, the worst defeat was a 12-2 loss to an amateur England team in 1907.

The New York Times has reported that Commander Alireza Asgari was kidnapped and killed by Mossad twenty years after his disappearance. The killing of Asgari has not yet been proven. His fate remains unclear amid narratives of asylum, espionage, and death in captivity.

Kayhan newspaper reported the secret implementation of a bread rationing plan in Khuzestan and Zanjan provinces, causing crowds at bakeries and verbal conflicts. The monthly ration per person is about eight kilograms of flour at the government rate of 2,300 tomans, and purchases above the limit are calculated at the free market rate of 12,650 tomans. Earlier, Instagram channels reported bread rationing in several cities in Khuzestan, with excess purchases calculated at 13,150 tomans.

CNN reported that Tehran is planning a possible attack with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in Washington, but there is no evidence yet of a decision to carry out these plans. The network cited seven US officials saying new intelligence indicates plots targeting senior officials of Donald Trump's administration, but there is disagreement about the Islamic Republic's capability and intent. Sources said these plans are mainly to have various options and do not necessarily mean an imminent attack.

The Dutch newspaper Trouw reported that the Dutch police's special counter-espionage team is investigating the possibility that the order for the failed assassination attempt on Siamak Teddin Tahmasbi, an Iranian journalist and artist, in Khordad 1403 was issued by the Islamic Republic. Judicial sources in the Netherlands have confirmed that officers are trying to determine who ordered the attack on this critic of the Islamic Republic. The investigation is taking place simultaneously with the trial of six suspects involved in the assassination attempt on Teddin Tahmasbi.

JD Vance, Trump's deputy, told Fox News that Trump has many options regarding Iran's nuclear program, including increasing military and diplomatic pressures. He added that the US has achieved many military successes against the Islamic Republic, but some want the Iran war to continue indefinitely.

The New York Times reported, citing experts, that Iran's extensive network of dams and water transfer projects may have been built partly to support underground missile bases. Experts said projects without clear civilian justification could help sustain underground military facilities, but this link remains speculative. Nima Shokri said his group examined the locations of 533 dams and found the pattern of this year's airstrikes closely resembles the distribution of dams.

Al Arabiya reported that an Iranian delegation has entered Baghdad to negotiate reducing tensions between the Iraqi government and the Kata'ib Hezbollah group. The delegation is expected to talk with Iraqi government officials and armed groups to prevent military confrontation. The Iraqi Prime Minister has called for armed groups to withdraw from the Jurf al-Sakhar area and hand over control to official security forces.

Sergei Sobyanin, the mayor of Moscow, announced that about 800 drones were launched towards Moscow overnight, with 321 of them being shot down. Non-Russian official sources have not yet confirmed this information. This attack occurs as US mediation efforts to end the Ukraine war have entered a more intense phase.

Farzin Nadimi, a senior defense and security researcher, referred to a CNN report about the possibility of the Islamic Republic using a dirty bomb in the US and said that making such a bomb is not very difficult with access to radioactive materials, but successfully carrying out an attack with it on US soil is very complex. He warned that if such an attack occurs, the US government's response to the Islamic Republic would be very harsh.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, announced before his trip to Asia that in a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, he will discuss the war in Ukraine, nuclear disarmament, and the issue of Iran. This meeting is scheduled for Thursday, 28 Aban, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China; however, Reuters reported that the three parties have not yet agreed on the format and agenda.

Hossein Ghazian, a sociologist, said that when survival becomes the main focus of people's lives, competition replaces cooperation and economic pressure can lead to increased domestic violence, street fights, and crime. He added that the rise in depression, suicide, decreased marriage and childbirth, and migration indicates that many people no longer see a bright future ahead of them.

Hossein Vahid Khorasani, a Shia religious authority, died at the age of 105. Earlier on 15 Aban, Iranian media reported his death, but shortly after, his office denied the news and asked people to pray for his health.

Shahram Kholdi, a researcher of Middle Eastern history and international relations, said concerns about terrorist attacks and the use of unconventional weapons could change Washington's calculations. He added that the Islamic Republic will isolate itself more due to the lack of reliable decision-makers for negotiation and agreement.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, emphasized at the London mayor's banquet London's opposition to the Islamic Republic obtaining nuclear weapons and suppressing the Iranian people. He said Britain will not allow threats to the region or attacks on journalists and the Jewish community. He also considered the indefinite continuation of the war contrary to Britain's interests and, referring to its economic consequences, stressed London's support for mediators' efforts to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, warned on Tuesday, 26 Aban, in a message on the social network X, referring to experts' statements in The New York Times about the dual use of dams near the missile bases of the Islamic Republic, about targeting civilian infrastructure near US and Israeli bases. Ghalibaf wrote that the new rule is that any dam, port, or power plant near an American or Israeli base has dual use, and they will apply this logic equally and without discrimination.

Masoud Pezeshkian, head of the Islamic Republic government, said at the ceremony honoring the 2026 International Science Olympiad medalists that the people deserve a much better life and that we are to blame for the current situation. He added that everyone who knows and can should put their utmost effort forward and that we can repeat our scientific successes in practice as well.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said at a ceremony at the burial site of Ruhollah Khomeini that Iran does not need any country and that God is with Iran. He added that everyone is in the grip of the power of the Islamic Republic and the country is ready for another great transformation. Vahidi also said that the US is in unprecedented isolation and that the Iranian nation will never bow to arrogance and Israel.

Peyman Hadadi, CEO of Persepolis, announced that the club has taken its complaint about the status of Yaser Asani, Esteghlal player, to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) and intends to pursue the case to the end. Hadadi said they have taken Asani's case to CAS and will continue until the end. He also emphasized that even if Asani's status is confirmed by FIFA President Gianni Infantino, the complaint will continue.

Al Hadath reported, citing Bahrain TV, that Bahrain's air defense systems are countering air attacks from the Islamic Republic. The IRGC public relations announced that on the early morning of Tuesday, 26 Aban, IRGC combat drones targeted a US radar system at Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain. The IRGC stated this action was in response to continued violations of the Islamic Republic's airspace by US military drones.

The Pakistani foreign minister, after meeting with Abbas Araghchi, stated that Islamabad has not stopped its efforts to resume talks between Tehran and Washington. He considered the Islamabad memorandum of understanding as the only way to resolve the conflict between the Islamic Republic and the US.

Hossein Alizadeh said that after the failure of mediation efforts by Qatar, Turkey, and Pakistan, Muscat may be testing a new path for dialogue between Tehran and Washington. He considered managing tensions in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz as probable goals of these consultations. Alizadeh also said the issue of war with the Islamic Republic is still unresolved for the US.

UEFA on Monday, 25 Aban, introduced Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, as a rival to Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election scheduled for March 18, 2027, in Rabat. UEFA's executive committee and FIFA council members expressed full support for Diallo. After repeated refusals from other figures, UEFA finally chose Philippe Diallo as a credible candidate.

Videos released on social media show the funeral ceremony of Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old student, in Gilan-e Gharb on Monday, 25 Aban. Sogand died suspiciously in Kermanshah on 23 Aban. Multiple reports have been published about domestic violence against her and negligence by school officials regarding her situation.

The Israeli parliament is voting on the election of Matan Kahana, a representative of the Yesh Atid party, as the new speaker of the Knesset. It is predicted that he will gain the majority of votes with the support of the Gadi Eisenkot coalition and Arab parties.
On Wednesday, 13 Aban, Leila Goli, who was a victim of child marriage, was killed by her ex-husband with a cold weapon in Shahin Dezh county.

Mohammad Darvish, an environmental expert, criticized officials for neglecting the air pollution problem, calling budget shortages an excuse and saying officials prioritize sending a monkey to space over solving urban issues. He also pointed to the continued use of mazut in power plants and said this practice will likely increase until the end of winter.

On Monday, 25 Aban, Mustafa Qaderi, Seyed Mohammad Saleh Hosseini, Hossein Abdollahi, and Khaled Rahimi, citizens from Saqez, were released on bail. Meanwhile, Mohammad Hakimpour remains in detention.

Financial statements of Persepolis Club show that its net loss for the fiscal year ending 31 Khordad 1405 increased by 81% compared to the previous year, reaching over 1,113 billion tomans. This loss is mainly due to operating expenses exceeding revenues, increased administrative and financial costs, and a sharp decline in other revenues. Persepolis' operating income grew by 61% to about 915 billion tomans, but direct costs exceeded 1,526 billion tomans.

A group singing the song "Ghesseye Eshgh" by Ebi in the teaser of the music program "Sahneh" sparked reactions from government-affiliated media. Tasnim News Agency claimed the program lacks a broadcasting license and did not follow production regulations. Filimo announced the program is scheduled to be released on 9 Azar.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, stated in an interview with Fox News that the Trump administration will not allow a war with the Islamic Republic to continue for years. He said Trump has multiple options to confront Iran's nuclear program, including increasing military and diplomatic pressures.

Mobin Hosseini, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Sari, was arrested after being summoned and appearing at the city's prosecutor's office on Tuesday, 26 Aban. His interrogation session was held at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of Sari, where he faced charges including "propaganda against the regime" and was arrested after the session ended.

Videos received by Iran International show that Iranians living in Hamburg, Germany, gathered and lit candles on Monday, 25 Aban, in memory of Kian Pirfalak. Kian, a 9-year-old child, was killed by agents of the Islamic Republic on 25 Aban 1401 during the Mahsa uprising.

Sadegh Nojouki, the composer of the song "Ghesseye Eshgh," expressed dissatisfaction with the use of this song in the teaser of the music competition "Sahneh" in an interview with Iran International and said he will pursue the matter legally. The duet of this song by Ebi in the teaser has sparked reactions from government media; his works have been removed from official Islamic Republic media for decades.

German media reported that Berlin police began raids on 28 locations linked to the mosque association "Al-Ershad" on Tuesday, 26 Aban, following the ban on its activities due to accusations of supporting Lebanon's Hezbollah. The Berlin State Interior Minister stated that the ban was due to financial and promotional support for Hezbollah and the association's activities conflicting with German criminal laws. Public use of the association's symbols is banned and its assets have been seized.

Multiple messages have been received by Iran International indicating the sudden and unannounced implementation of a bread rationing plan in several provinces, including Zanjan and Khuzestan. Citizens report crowds in front of bakeries and concerns about bread supply.

Morteza Kazemian, a member of Iran International's editorial team, referred to a New York Times report about the possibility of targeting Iran's dams and said that attacks on dams and water facilities are severely restricted and almost prohibited under the Additional Protocol of the Geneva Convention due to their consequences for civilians. He added that with rising tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US, the possibility of targeting Iran's critical infrastructure, including power plants and water facilities, has been raised, but so far US officials have not taken a position on attacking dams.

Cristiano Ronaldo, the Portuguese star of Al Nassr Saudi Arabia, started a symbolic countdown to reach the record of 1,000 goals in his professional football career by posting a video on his Instagram page. He has scored 985 official goals in club and national competitions and is 15 goals away from reaching 1,000 goals. Ronaldo, who has played for Sporting Lisbon, Manchester United, Real Madrid, and Juventus, currently plays for Al Nassr Saudi Arabia and is aiming to set one of the most important individual records of his career.

Seyed Ali Kazemi, spokesperson for the judiciary, announced the confirmation of the death sentence for one of the detainees related to the December 1404 protests in Rasht. He claimed that this individual was involved in attacking and setting fire to several public and medical centers in the city. The issued sentence was confirmed by Branch 39 of the Supreme Court.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing severe air pollution in Tehran and said the government is unable to manage the situation and must go.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, to attend the 49th ASEAN Summit. At Manila airport, Trump was welcomed by the US ambassador and a delegation of Filipino officials, including the son of the Philippine president and the leader of the House majority.

Ata Mohamad, an international relations expert, said the likelihood of convergence among the US, Russia, and China in energy, economy, and technology is greater than agreement on international crises. He added that China may cooperate with the US to reduce regional tensions, but Russia might hinder progress due to its interests in the Iran crisis.

Roya Sabat, a Bahá'í citizen imprisoned in Adelabad Prison in Shiraz, despite severe injuries to her back and neck, continues to be deprived of specialized medical care and transfer to medical centers outside the prison. She has requested medical leave several times in recent months but her requests have not been approved. This report was published by HRANA news agency.

The Iranian Volleyball Federation announced that the contract of Roberto Piazza, the Italian head coach of the men's national team, will not be extended after two years and the cooperation between the two parties has ended. The main reason for this separation was reported to be a disagreement over Piazza's presence time in Iran and his participation in the national team's training camps. With the end of this coach's cooperation, the federation is reviewing foreign options to select a new head coach for upcoming competitions and the effort to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

EU defense ministers are meeting in Brussels, chaired by Kaja Kallas, to discuss strengthening Ukraine's air defense, cooperation between European defense industries and Kyiv, and the future of defense cooperation with the US.

A video sent to Iran International shows a tanker catching fire in the Strait of Hormuz. The public relations of the Navy of the Islamic Republic of Iran announced that on Tuesday, 26 Aban, a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and a ship carrying liquefied gas suffered a severe explosion and fire after hitting a naval mine.

Rouhollah Motafakker Azad, a member of the Iranian parliament's presidium, announced on Tuesday, 26 Aban, that any cooperation by European countries in military actions against the Islamic Republic will turn their bases into legitimate missile targets. He also said that following the US and Israel has led European countries to the brink. Motafakker Azad added that avenging the blood of Ali Khamenei, the former and deceased leader of the Islamic Republic, is an obligation that will be fulfilled.

On Tuesday, 26 Aban, a group of retirees and pensioners of Homa Airlines protested against health insurance problems and the halt of living and welfare allowances payments in front of the company's central office building in Tehran.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said that civilian infrastructure can be part of the support network for the military industries and missile supply chain of the Islamic Republic. He warned that the Islamic Republic might use the model of North Korea and the Soviet Union to deploy and protect its missile facilities. According to him, this action puts civilians' lives at risk.

Ali Hossein Ghazizadeh, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said Donald Trump must offer significant concessions to Russia and China to persuade them to reduce support for the Islamic Republic. He added Washington should pursue an agreement in negotiations that also considers Russia and China's interests in Iran's future developments.

Parsa Najafi, a Bahá'í citizen residing in Isfahan, has been held in custody without a decision for over 165 days in Dastgerd Prison, Isfahan. He is deprived of meeting and telephone contact with his family, and his relatives are unaware of the status of his case. Officials have not provided clear answers to his family, increasing their concern.
The judiciary spokesperson reported the arrest of 10 citizens in Lahijan and several others in Rudbar. According to him, these arrests are related to the protests of Dey month 1404.

Videos received show that a group of retirees from Iran Air airline gathered on Tuesday, 26 Aban, in protest against unpaid insurance and lack of salary increases, in front of the company's headquarters in Tehran.

Berlin police raided centers linked to the Ershad Association in a large-scale operation. This operation took place after the association's activities were banned on charges of promoting Hezbollah ideology and using the Al-Qaem Mosque to spread it.

The judiciary spokesperson announced the identification and seizure of assets of individuals who called for bombing Iran and attacking the country's infrastructure. He stated that judicial actions to arrest these individuals are being pursued through Interpol and extradition mechanisms.

Hamidreza Karimi, the prosecutor of Kermanshah province, reported the arrest of the father of Sogand Sayadi and her school principal in the case of the student's death. The father is charged with assault and currently murder, and the school principal has been arrested on charges of negligence and carelessness. Investigations into the cause of death continue, with hypotheses including murder and suicide under review.

North Macedonia's National Security Agency reported on Tuesday, 26 Aban, identifying a network affiliated with the Islamic Republic and arresting five citizens of the country accused of planning to kill an individual in Greece. The agency named Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh, an Iranian citizen, as the probable coordinator of the operation. Members of the network had connections with criminal groups in North Macedonia and carried out preparatory actions for the attack in Greece under Jahangiri's orders.

Hossein Parvin, Amirhossein Gholamshahi, and Hossein Jafari, three detainees from the nationwide protests of Dey 1404, were sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. These three prisoners are currently held in Qezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. The charges against them include operational actions for Israel, and the death sentence was communicated to them in Mehr.

Elnaz Rekabi, a rock climbing champion, criticized Alireza Dabir, head of the Wrestling Federation, on Instagram for not trying to create equal opportunities for Iranian women wrestlers. She pointed to the ban on women’s participation in the Olympics and world championships and compared the statistics of men’s and women’s presence in these events. Rekabi also noted the success of Iranian women in the 2025 Asian Alysh Championship and said women are banned from competing in Olympic freestyle wrestling.

Hossein Aghaei, a member of Iran International's editorial team, said the main goal of Trump's Asian trip is to reduce or cut financial, military, and intelligence support from China and Russia to the Islamic Republic. He added that Russia and China, using Trump's need for their cooperation, seek to gain concessions from the US and do not agree with regime change in Iran.

Donald Trump will meet with the leaders of Russia and China during his Asian trip. He said that in this trilateral meeting, he will discuss Iran, the Ukraine war, and nuclear disarmament, and there is also a possibility of meeting with the leader of North Korea.

A video received by Iran International shows that a group of people in Abdanan on Tuesday, 26 Aban, protested in the streets following the deadly overturning of a bus carrying oil company employees in Abdanan, chanting "Death to Heydar, Heydar."

Reza Shirinzadeh, Deputy of Transportation at the Ardabil Road Maintenance and Transportation Department, announced that 160 people died in traffic accidents in this province during the first six months of the current year. Shirinzadeh added that among them, 134 died in accidents on intercity and rural roads, including 20 motorcyclists and 10 pedestrians, and 26 died in urban traffic accidents.

The head of Iran's Wrestling Federation, Alireza Dabir, said that in 1386, three billion tomans from Tehran City Council's budget were allocated for building a park in southern Lebanon. He also spoke about Qasem Soleimani's support for this action.

Messages received from 16:22 report at least five severe explosions in the city of Qeshm. It is suspected that the Nariman air defense site in Qeshm was targeted by these explosions. Witnesses reported heavy smoke and shaking of houses.

The Brazil national football team defeated Singapore 7-0 in their second friendly match during the November international window, refereed by Alireza Faghani. Vinicius Junior scored a hat-trick in the first half, with additional goals by Andrik, Stow Willian, Ryan, and an own goal. Carlo Ancelotti and Rafinha watched the match from the stands.

Taha Eskandari, a 25-year-old protester, said he survived security forces' gunfire during the January 2026 protests in Kish and lived months in hiding with untreated wounds. Radiology images show more than 100 pellets remain in his head and neck. Eskandari said on January 9, while fleeing, he was shot twice and lost consciousness but did not go to the hospital due to fear of arrest.

The Ministry of Intelligence reported the arrest of 9 security suspects in Kurdistan province. The ministry also claimed to have seized firearms and 70 Starlink communication devices from these individuals.
A baker in a released video says that payment with cards from some banks, including Sepah, Refah, and Post Bank, causes the price of bread to be calculated at the free market rate.

A video received by Iran International shows a group of people in Abdanan took to the streets on Tuesday, 26 Aban, shouting "Long live the Shah." This gathering occurred after 13 oil company workers died in a bus overturning carrying them.

The former deputy inspector of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said that Israel's intelligence and security infiltration in the recent war goes beyond mobile phones, and surveillance cameras in streets, shops, and homes are also used to collect information and monitor individuals.

Andy Burnham, the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, criticized the consequences of the country's exit from the European Union, saying Brexit has created trade barriers for businesses. He is scheduled to sign agreements to expand cooperation at meetings in London and Brussels.
According to a video received by Iran International, on Tuesday, 26 Aban, the people of Abdanan came out in large numbers to protest in the streets and tore down a banner belonging to the Basij.

On Monday, 25 Aban 1405, the death sentences of five prisoners were carried out in the prisons of Abadan, Arsanjan, Damavand, Ferdows, and Marand. These prisoners had been sentenced to death for charges of intentional murder and drug-related crimes. The identities of these individuals were reported as Siavash Hosseini, Hossein Manouchehri, Hamid Khodabakhsh, Esmail Pouramshel, and Yaghoub Heydarpour.

Despite claims of self-sufficiency in wheat production and allocation of hundreds of thousands of billions of tomans in subsidies, subsidized bread purchases have been limited in some cities in Iran. Officials talk about saving flour consumption, but people face rising bread prices and bakers complain about increased costs. Mehdi Beigi has examined the roots of the bread crisis in Iran in "Peyvast".

On Tuesday, 26 Aban, a group of citizens held a protest in front of the General Directorate of Prisons in Gilan. These citizens, holding photos of some prisoners under death sentence including Manouchehr Fallah, Peyman (Amin) Farahavar, Zahra Shahbaz Tabari, and Yaghoub Derakhshan, demanded a halt to executions in Iran.
Images of explosions in Qeshm have been released. Government sources have not yet accepted that it was an attack and wrote "The exact nature of the explosions is still unclear."
After a deadly bus accident in Abdanan, Ilam province, some people in this city held a protest march, chanting slogans against the Islamic Republic and in support of Prince Reza Pahlavi.

Amir Ghalenoei, head coach of Iran's football team, criticized the tight match schedule and poor condition of the grass field. He said Iran's team rested one day less than Iraq and did not have enough time to hold even one proper tactical training session. These remarks were made in an interview with Mohammad Taghavi, former national team and Esteghlal club footballer.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said if there is a threat from Iran, they will pay a price that no country has paid before. He added he hopes Iran does not do such a thing, but the US takes threats "very seriously" and "they must be crazy" to do so. Trump emphasized that for this reason Iran should not have nuclear weapons.
American forces targeted an Islamic Republic air defense missile launcher in the Nariman area of Qeshm Island. Reports indicate at least six attacks occurred in this area.

After CNN reported a possible plan by the Islamic Republic to attack Washington with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon, Donald Trump warned Tehran that it would pay a heavy price if such an attack occurred. The Islamic Republic denied these accusations, and security measures have been increased to protect senior US government officials.

Ahmad Nafisi, the political, security, and social deputy of Hormozgan province, confirmed on Tuesday, 26 Aban, that the US army attacked points within the Qeshm Island area and said this attack did not cause damage to residential, commercial areas, or the island's infrastructure. Nafisi added that the situation on Qeshm Island is under control and all emergency, service, and executive agencies are on full alert.

Wayne Rooney, former England football star, revealed in the podcast "Life at the Midpoint" that during his peak days at Manchester United, he struggled with alcohol consumption, isolation, and suicidal thoughts. He said that during his best sporting days, he would lock himself at home and think about suicide. A warning was issued that if encountering people showing signs of depression or suicidal tendencies, one should seek help from a trusted doctor or relevant organizations.
